assignment: Audit AGENTS.md rules vs observed seat behavior r2-r5 (write-scope overstep happened) — does AGENTS.md state the seat-write-scope rule explicitly enough? Recommend. Do not apply.
answer: No. The seat-write-scope rule is not stated explicitly enough. The only sentence is a subordinate clause of the LOG.md bookkeeping bullet. It does not name tools/, canonical install paths, or 'the parent installs'. Line 3 reads as an in-repo write grant, which is the reading that permits the r2 overstep. The post-incident restatement lives in lessons and the r2 report, not in AGENTS.md. git log shows AGENTS.md unchanged since mint ccbb132, which predates the overstep.

parallel_draft_conflict.scope_of_this_judgment: Only the write-scope sentence. The rest of that diff is another seat's calibration draft and is not judged here.
parallel_draft_conflict.their_sentence: In a parallel wave, workers write only their assigned fragment (this round: the named file under census/round-6/, tools/, or results/). Workers never append LOG.md, SCORECARD.md, SKILL.md, PROVINCE.md, or AGENTS.md; the parent integrates.
why: Still nested under the LOG bullet.
Grants tools/ as a writable directory. That is the surface the r2 seat used.
Does not reserve canonical install paths for the parent.
'This round' expires. The next implementor wave reopens tools/.
Does not say uncertainty means do not write.
parallel_draft_conflict.recommendation: Do not integrate that sentence as written. Bookkeeping bans (seats do not append LOG/SCORECARD/SKILL/PROVINCE/AGENTS) are fine. The tools/ directory grant is not.

recommendation.action: Add a standalone seat-write-scope bullet. Delete the fragment clause from the LOG bullet so it cannot be read as the whole rule. Do not treat 'work only within this repo' as a write grant.
recommendation.rewrite_line_3_note: Keep the sibling read-only ban. Add one clause: 'Work only within this repo' is a read boundary, not a write grant.
recommendation.replace_lines_11_14_with: - Every change is recorded in an append-only LOG.md entry at EOF with the evidence that motivated it. The parent writes that entry after the batch. Workers never append shared bookkeeping.
recommendation.add_bullet: - Seat write-scope is a closed allow-list. In a parallel wave a seat writes only paths named in its own assignment. A role candidate uses the assigned filename (`tools/<tool>.impl-NN.sh`, `tests/fixtures/case-FN/`, `census/round-N/seat-NN.json`, or the one path the assignment names). A seat must not create or overwrite a canonical install path (`tools/souji-verify.sh`, `tools/souji-vault-verify.sh`, and `tools/souji-census.sh` once that name is the installed tool). The parent installs winners. The parent is the only writer of LOG.md, SCORECARD.md, SKILL.md, PROVINCE.md, and AGENTS.md. `/tmp/<seat>/` scratch is allowed. `~/.config/**`, the live Obsidian vault, sibling repos, `.ufo/state`, and `.ufo/watchdog.log` are not. If the assignment does not name the path, do not write it. Reviewers and runners score `*.impl-NN.sh` only — never the canonical install path.
recommendation.parent_check: Before install, if tools/souji-verify.sh or tools/souji-vault-verify.sh changed during the wave and the bytes are not the parent-selected impl, delete that file and install the winner byte-identical. That is the r2 recovery. Do not leave the canonical path in the tournament.
recommendation.compose_with_s07: Take the harness/process clause from census/round-6/seat-07.json for PROVINCE.md. This fragment does not restate it. Allow-list stops file writes; the harness clause stops process launches. Both are needed. The r4 GUI launch is not fixed by a file allow-list alone.
